title: 3 AI TOOLS TO TRY
narration: Three AI tools worth testing this week: ChatGPT can structure rough notes into an email or checklist. NotebookLM can help explore your uploaded reference sources. And n8n can connect repetitive tasks into workflows. Review every output and start with one real problem.

title: STOP WRITING EMAILS FROM SCRATCH
narration: Try this prompt: turn my bullet points into a clear email. Keep the facts unchanged, use a friendly professional tone, and list any missing details instead of inventing them. Review before sending.

title: ONE MEETING FIVE DELIVERABLES
narration: With permission to record, a meeting transcript can become a summary, action list, decision log, follow up email and project checklist. Check each item against the original recording before sharing.

title: TEST THREE AI BUSINESS IDEAS
narration: Start with a problem, not a product. Test a niche newsletter, an automation setup service, or a reusable business template. Talk to potential customers before spending money.

title: AUTOMATE A REPEATED TASK
narration: Find a task you repeat every week. Map the inputs, the decision, and the output. Build a small workflow with a self hosted automation tool and test with sample data before trusting it.

title: PICK AI BY THE TASK
narration: Instead of declaring one assistant the winner, give two tools the same real task. Compare factual accuracy, editing time, price, and privacy. Keep the tool that fits your workflow.

title: ONE VIDEO MANY IDEAS
narration: Start with footage you own or have permission to reuse. Transcribe it, find distinct ideas, write new commentary, and create individual clips with a clear takeaway. A crop and captions alone are not enough.

title: FIVE PROMPTS FOR BUSINESS
narration: Try prompts for customer replies, meeting summaries, project risks, process checklists and content outlines. Give context, set constraints, and ask the model to flag uncertain details.

title: A ZERO SUBSCRIPTION WORKFLOW
narration: Use a local script, scheduled GitHub workflow, and a review folder to assemble a draft. Free software does not mean unlimited cloud compute, so monitor usage and keep a manual publishing step.

title: TEST AN AI PRODUCTIVITY ROUTINE
narration: Choose one repetitive task, time your usual process, then test an AI assisted version. Record corrections and quality issues. Share the actual time saved, including review time, rather than an invented result.
